question: Which exact 3.101.036 callable sets LVGL label long mode for circular title scrolling?
callsite_evidence: Exact 3.101.036 sub_C588BC0 is called with a live label in R0 and small LVGL long-mode enum values in R1 throughout stock UI code.
Stock create_long_label helper sub_C522460 creates a label, applies style, calls sub_C588BC0(label, 0), sets width 304 and then assigns text, confirming the two-argument label/long-mode ABI.
Its exact 3.101.043 counterpart includes a stock mode-3 caller, and LVGL v9 defines mode 3 as LV_LABEL_LONG_SCROLL_CIRCULAR.
control_flow_evidence: 3.101.036 sub_C588BC0 and exact 3.101.043 sub_C588BF8 are byte-identical eight-byte Thumb veneers to the same platform callable 0x1C06F15D.
3.101.036 sub_C522460 and 3.101.043 sub_C543748 are both 0x5E-byte, eight-block create_long_label helpers with corresponding call order and argument flow.
The exact 3.101.036 veneer entry is 0x0C588BC0 and its Thumb callable address is 0x0C588BC1.
ownership_analysis: The function borrows a live LVGL label and changes its long-mode state without retaining or freeing it. Calls remain on the UI owner thread.
unsafe_assumptions: The existing 3.101.036 UI path is known working, but the newly selected circular mode still requires a long-title device rendering probe.
The label must have finite one-line geometry before circular scrolling is enabled.
recommended_probe: On exact 3.101.036, compare short and over-width titles, verify circular scrolling and fixed author placement, then switch tracks and destroy/reopen the page.
